observations:
Torah #138 is an extremely brief Torah (6 lines) that has not yet been encoded in torahData.js at all — it has zero edges in the dataset.

The Torah's teaching is structurally simple and compact: it presents a single unified conceptual cluster centered on the heart (לֵב) as the dwelling place of the divine essence, with one explicit bechina (bar levav = chalal libo) and one eitza result (knowing the future).

Two packages were proposed:
  Package 1 — הַלֵּב וּדְבַר ה' (The Heart and the Word of God) [good] — the primary teaching cluster
  Package 2 — יְדִיעַת עֲתִידוֹת (Knowledge of the Future) [good] — the eitza terminus

These two packages fully cover all seven conceptual nodes derivable from this Torah. No additional bechina domain of 3+ concepts was found that is structurally separate and not already covered.

Regarding the good/evil mirror structure: Torah #138 does not develop an explicit evil mirror. The Torah is entirely affirmative — it teaches what the heart CAN do when it is hollow and pure. The implicit negative counterpart (the 'filled' or arrogant heart that cannot receive divine speech) is not elaborated or given its own bechina vocabulary in this text. No evil package is warranted.

The cross-reference to Torah #49 ('כַּמְבֹאָר אֶצְלֵנוּ בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר לעיל בסימן מט') indicates that the deeper development of the לֵב = עִקַּר הָאֱלֹקוּת principle belongs to Torah #49's package system. Torah #138 is a very concise summary/restatement of that principle with the specific application to prophetic knowledge of the future.

The Torah's argument in one move:
  [Pkg 1: The hollow heart receives divine speech] —eitza→ [Pkg 2: Prophetic knowledge of the future]

No new packages are needed beyond the two already proposed in torah_138_packages.json.
